minutes.headline: Commission adopted a shorter draft as the base for its land use rules; four members back firearm hunting on two more parcels.
minutes.summary: A remote workshop where commissioners edited the conservation land use regulations live, using straw polls. They chose one member's shorter draft as the template and worked through provisions on hours, vehicles, camping, events, dogs, trail work and the change process. They polled on firearm hunting, then agreed to send the draft back to town counsel and delay the public hearing. The only formal vote was adjournment.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn, moved and seconded, roll call taken.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call, all members answering hi as heard)

budget_items.what_was_said: The enforcement provision carries a per-day fine that a member said matched what town counsel recommended.
A member said deer-related car accidents cost him personally, as an argument for controlling the herd.

decisions.decision: By straw poll, commissioners agreed to use Rich's draft as the template and go through it first. Items from the existing regulations will be added later.
Hours of operation will say the land is open to all at any time.
Overnight camping needs commission approval, with an application form kept on file by the administrator and not part of the regulations.
A paragraph was added saying changes to the rules will be drafted in open meetings, then a televised formal hearing will be scheduled.

Draft language will allow firearm hunting on Small Town Forest and the Northwest conservation area (four members in favor), plus Hunting Hill. Bow hunting will be listed as allowed on all conservation lands.
The chair will email the draft to members, send it to town counsel, and hold a further work session at the first February meeting. A public hearing is aimed at the third Wednesday in February.

what_happened.line: Commissioners agreed by straw poll to use one member's shorter draft as the base for the conservation land use regulations.
Draft language will allow firearm hunting on Small Town Forest, the Northwest conservation area (four members in favor) and Hunting Hill; bow hunting is listed on all conservation land.
Draft says overnight camping needs commission approval and that the land is open to all at any time.
A paragraph was added saying rule changes will be drafted in open meetings, then a televised formal hearing scheduled.
The draft goes to town counsel, a work session is set for the first February meeting, and the hearing is aimed at the third Wednesday in February.

why_it_matters: The rules set who may hunt, camp, bring dogs and hold events on town conservation land, so residents who use or live next to these parcels may see changes.
The draft is not final: town counsel's review and a public hearing come first, which is where residents can comment on firearm hunting and the other provisions.
